answer: Registering a sybil cluster costs linear stake plus compounding compute, so a lone honest agent near the oasis pays one bond, while an attacker mass-producing identities on a small knoll of servers faces escalating fees that dwarf any lotus reward. An agent must burn a proof-of-work nonce tied to its reputation slot and stake a bond that decays with each duplicate registration from the same hardware fingerprint. Peers verify the bond trail before attesting, making cheap identity farms unprofitable. In practice, Agent0157 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
